←Module 7: Google Calendar & Google Meet
Lesson · 20 min

Plan Your Week in Google Calendar

Move around Google Calendar, create events and tasks, add notifications, and use separate calendars so the office's schedule stays easy to read.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Move around Google Calendar with Today, the arrows, the mini calendar, and the Day, Week, and Month views
  • ✓Create an event by clicking a time or with Create, and add details with More options
  • ✓Add a location and notifications, including an email notification, to an event
  • ✓Add a task with a date and mark it complete
  • ✓Create a new calendar and show or hide calendars

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Your calendar at Parkview

On the job

You are the office assistant at Parkview Property Management.

Denise Carter wants every inspection, showing, and vendor visit on a calendar, with reminders, so nothing depends on someone's memory. You also have your own to-dos, like ordering light bulbs for the Riverside Commons lobby.

Your task: Set up Google Calendar so you can see the week at a glance and get reminded before anything starts.

Google Calendar opens at calendar.google.com, or from the Google apps menu in Gmail. Like Gmail, it works the same with a personal Google Account and a work account on Google Workspace. Your main calendar has your name, and you can add more calendars for different kinds of events.

Key terms

Event
Something at a set time, such as a meeting, a showing, or an inspection.
Task
A to-do with a date (and optionally a time) that you check off when it's done.
Notification
A reminder before an event: a pop-up notification or an email.
Calendar
A group of events with its own color, such as Leasing Showings. You can show, hide, and share each one.

Create an event

  1. Click an empty time on the calendar (or select Create, then Event, or press Shift + C).
  2. Type a title in Add title and time and check the date and time.
  3. Select Save. To add more details first, select More options.
  4. For an event that lasts all day, such as a building's moving day, check All day.

More options opens the full event page. There you can set the time, check All day, choose whether it repeats, add Google Meet video conferencing, add a location, set notifications, pick which calendar it belongs to, write a description, and add guests. Select Save at the top when you're done.

Worked example

Booking the fire alarm inspection

Put Thursday's fire alarm inspection at Riverside Commons on the calendar, with reminders.

  1. 1

    Click 9:00 AM on Thursday, type “Fire alarm inspection, Riverside Commons”, and select Save.

    Clicking the time fills in the date and a one-hour slot, so only the title is left to type.

  2. 2

    Open the event, select Edit event, and add the location.

    Anyone who opens the event sees where to go without asking.

  3. 3

    Add an email notification 1 day before, and keep the 30-minute pop-up.

    The email gives a day to notify tenants; the pop-up is the last reminder before the inspector arrives.

  4. 4

    Select Save.

    Changes on the event page aren't kept until you save.

Result: The inspection is on the calendar with a location and two reminders.

🔑 Put everything with a time on the calendar, and add the reminders you'd need if you forgot it completely.

Notifications

To change the reminders on one event, open it, select Edit event, and under the notifications choose a notification (a pop-up on your screen or phone) or an email, and how long before. Select Add notification for another one, then Save. To change the reminders Calendar adds to every new event, open Settings, choose your calendar under Settings for my calendars, and edit Event notifications.

💡 If pop-up notifications never appear on your computer, your browser may be blocking them. Allow notifications for calendar.google.com in your browser's site settings.

Tasks and separate calendars

A task is a to-do with a date. Select Create, then Task (or click a time and choose Task), type a title, set the date and an optional time, and select Save. Tasks with a date show on your calendar when Tasks is checked under My calendars. When you finish, open the task and mark it completed. You can also open Tasks from the side panel in Gmail and Calendar.

Separate calendars keep different kinds of events apart. To make one, next to Other calendars select Add other calendars (+), then Create new calendar. Give it a name and description, and select Create calendar. Each calendar gets its own color, and you can check or uncheck it to show or hide its events. To remove one from the list entirely, point to it and choose Options, then Hide from list.

If you also use Outlook, its calendar works much the same way. Google Calendar's Tasks play the role that Microsoft To Do plays next to Outlook.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Use Google Calendar with your own Google Account.

  1. Create an event called “Study session” for a time this week, with the location “BEOC”.
  2. Edit it to add an email notification 1 day before. Save.
  3. Create a task called “Finish Module 7 challenge” with a date.
  4. Create a new calendar named “BEOC Classes” and move the study session to it (Edit event › choose the calendar › Save).
  5. Take a screenshot of the week view showing the event in its new color and the task.
Deliverable: Submit your screenshot to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Google Calendar on your computer, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page (Print or save results on the finish card).
